entry_points.text: Bring-up adds a disk with no parent, allocates with caller limits and node, and registers a major; holder link and unlink in this build are no-ops reporting success.
In this configuration invalidation and stat do nothing, single-device sync and flush report success, and discard converts blocks to sectors and delegates.
IO waiter wakes self directly or another task, bio accounting forwards with stored device and start time, splitting delegates by limits alignment, and crypto registration reports success.
Top-level search delegates with null root and iterators walk arrays, children and key-value pairs; exit reports absent in this build.
Group lock init prepares every array element; superblock open requests read with restricted writes plus write unless read-only; compat pointer helper is null.
Lifecycle management is inert here: attach, detach, link and query fail invalid argument, and storage alloc and free are no-effect.

exports.text: Queue state is exposed through single-flag predicates for dying, init done, quiesced, registered and related dispatch modes; each reports whether its flag is set.
Capability and limit queries read queue feature bits and size fields, covering rotational, zoned, multiqueue, max sectors, physical block size and stable writes.
Zoned helpers map sectors to zone numbers, report counts and capacities, detect straddles, and treat append as emulated when zoned without hardware support.
Bio iteration walks linked bios, request lookup recovers the request from its queue node, vector mapping maps one slice for DMA, and boundary helper reports sectors to the next boundary.

Drivers use a block operations table for submission, open, ioctls, geometry and zones, plus holder callbacks for dead, sync, freeze and thaw, and an IO batch grouping requests with timestamp and poll context, with a declaration helper for default init.
Cgroup filters expose inbound and outbound packet verdicts gated on global and per-socket activity with full-socket checks, plus creation and connect runners that fix the attach type.
Address filtering offers unlocked and socket-locked forms with bind flag exemption, alongside socket-ops, device and get-option hooks; get-option preserves its input result.

hazards.text: Updating elevator or queue count without freezing races attributes and limit changes outside the mutex race readers; swap free runs under swap locks; skipping plugging or straddle checks misroutes zone writes and tail capacity must be used at device end.
Egress and sock-ops revalidate full-socket identity and packet-socket agreement, and ingress requires non-null full socket, preventing filtering on half-initialized or released views.
Queue, trace, boot and BPF helpers rely on external atomic, bit, log, math, min-max, mutex and RCU helpers owned elsewhere.

invariants.text: Alloc-time, power-status and zoned queries have dual builds: one reads live state, the other reports fixed inactive values when the feature is compiled out.

Zone write plugging applies only to writes on plugged disks for a closed set of zone operations, excluding flushes and already-marked bios; atomic writes need nonzero hardware minimum with partition alignment.
Integrity size is capped by segment size and metadata interval; trace sector helpers report zero for passthrough or unset positions, and group-to-lock mapping masks the group number.
Bootconfig value versus key follows the data high bit, arrays and leaves follow child shape, and checksum sums all input bytes from zero.

Cgroup attachment enumerates from invalid through socket and network lifecycle to device and LSM range; socket enablement compares against the shared empty array and static branches gate hooks, with conversion mapping recognized types or invalid.
With cgroup BPF compiled out every hook evaluates neutral without touching arguments except get-option which preserves its input; core headers use once-only guards.

locks.text: Queue tail splits duties: elevator mutex for scheduler and related attrs with freeze-before-take order, limits mutex for limits and read-ahead with start returning a copy and cancel releasing.
Holder callbacks release the device holder lock on return; enabled trace paths hold read protection while loading the trace pointer; bottom-half disable balances preempt count with barrier.
Locking address helpers hold the socket lock only around the filter call after confirming enablement, releasing before interpreting results so caller flag updates happen unlocked.

state_machines.text: Queue moves through init done to registered to quiesced, with dying marking teardown; registered means attached and quiesced means suspended dispatch.
When tracing is enabled message helpers forward if a trace object exists and notify bit is set; disabled builds turn setup, start-stop and removal into errors and message helpers into no-ops.

structs.text: Queue tail holds elevator, sysfs, limits and freeze mutexes, unused-context list with spinlock, freeze depth and waitqueue, tag set, debug dentries and RCU head; flag order runs dying through zoned writes to a max sentinel with multiqueue default selecting same-completion; default limits are 128 segments, 255 sectors and 64k segment size.

Trace descriptor holds version, state, relay channel, per-cpu sequences, action mask, ranges, ids, dentry, list and drops; compat setup carries device, mask, buffers, addresses and pid; max note is 128 bytes and compat setup uses magic 0x18 number 115.
Compat partition arg carries op, flags, length and pointer; group locking uses a lock array sized by count with single versus scaled sizing; integrity payload max is 2MB.
Bootconfig nodes pack four 16-bit indices; magic length is 12 with 4-byte alignment; key marker is zero and data caps bound the tree.
Full cgroup state holds per-type arrays, lists, flags and release work; storage groups refcounted buffers, map descriptors and links; LSM slots are 10 in the full variant.

Map operations centralize alloc, lookup, update, delete, batch, queue, percpu, fd translation, codegen, mmap, poll, storage charging, redirect and iteration; iter support defines callback and sequence info with ops and private size.

BTF field kinds are powers of two; each field has offset, size and kind with pointer or graph metadata; records hold counts, masks, cached offsets and flexible fields; list and rbnodes pair linkage with owner and 8-byte alignment.
Unique-id types number T10 one, EUI64 two and NAA three; zeroing flags occupy bits 0 to 2 for nounmap, nofallback and killable; poll oneshot is bit 0.
